newsitem.title: EU: EC Report Weekly Diary for Monday, May 5-Sunday, May 11.
newsitem.headline: EC Report Weekly Diary for Monday, May 5-Sunday, May 11.

text.p: HIGHLIGHTS

BRUSSELS - Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen meets European Commission President Santer and other Commission members (Monday); discussions to cover state of the inter-governmental conference on EU treaty reforms, economic and monetary union, EU enlargement and the EU's northern dimension.
BRUSSELS - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting (Tuesday).
LUXEMBOURG - NATO and Russia hold a new round of talks in an attempt to strike a deal on a new post-Cold War pact (Tuesday).
Thursday - EU institutions closed for Ascension holiday.
Friday - EU institutions closed for "Robert Schuman" remembrance day.
BRUSSELS - Open house at European Union buildings (Saturday).
MONDAY, MAY 5

BRUSSELS - Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen meets European Commission President Santer and Commissioners de Silguy, Oreja and Bjerregaard; discussions to cover state of the inter-governmental conference on EU treaty reforms, economic and monetary union, EU enlargement and the EU's northern dimension.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Parliament Agriculture Committee meets (0900/0700 GMT).

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Peripheral Maritime Regions of Europe (CRPM) holds news conference on the outcome of meetings with European Commissioners Oreja, de Silguy and Wulf-Mathies (1800/1600 GMT). Venue: Fondation Galice Europe, avenue Milcamps 105. Contact: Foundation Galice Europe (32 2) 735 5440.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Global Legislators Organisation for a Balanced Environment (GLOBE) - uniting legislators from Europe, Japan, Russia, the United States, Southern Africa and Latin America - holds its 12th general assembly (to Wednesday). Discussions include concrete actions to implement the decisions of the Earth Summit held in Rio in June 1992; endocrine disrupting chemicals. Speakers include: European Parliament deputies Tom Spencer and Ken Collins. Venue: European Parliament, Espace Leopold 07C50. Contact: GLOBE (322) 230 6589.

BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - Euro Citizen Action Service (ECAS) holds conference on "Preparing Citizens' Europe Day: EU Citizenship - current state and future perspectives" in cooperation with the European Parliament and European Commission (0900/0700 GMT) (and Tuesday). Venue: European Parliament, Van Maerlandt II. Contact: Jessica Erbe, ECAS (322) 548 9821.
INNSBRUCK, Austria - EU Committee of the Regions holds seminar on "Transport policy for sensitive areas". Contact: Committee of the Regions (322) 282 2155.
TUESDAY, MAY 6

BRUSSELS - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting. Provisional agenda includes reports and proposals on EU fight against fraud and corruption - followed by a news conference by Commissioner Anita Gradin.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Parliament Agriculture Committee meets (0900/0700 GMT).

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Global Legislators Organisation for a Balanced Environment (GLOBE) holds its 12th general assembly (second of three days). News conference at 1100/0900 GMT. Venue: European Parliament, Espace Leopold.
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - Euro Citizen Action Service (ECAS) holds conference on "EU Citizenship - current state and future perspectives" (0900/0700 GMT) (second of two days).

BRUSSELS - European Institute for Asian Studies holds lunchtime meeting on "The Burmese economy and the GSP case" covering the EU's Generalised System of Preferences trade scheme (1230/1030 GMT). Venue: European Institute for Asian Studies, 35 rue des Deux Eglises. Contact: Zoe McCarthy, European Insitute for Asian Studies (322) 230 8122.

LOUVAIN-LA-NEUVE (NEW ITEM) - European Studies Institute holds round table on "The fathers of Europe" (1800/1600 GMT); Societe General Chairman Etienne Davignon chairs the meeting. Venue: Auditoire Socrate, place Cardinal Mercier. Contact: European Studies Institute (3210) 47 85 45.
LUXEMBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov begins official visit (to Wednesday).

LUXEMBOURG - NATO and Russia hold a new round of talks in an attempt to strike a deal on a new post-Cold War pact. NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana and Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov attend.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Federation of Building Societies holds news conference on the occasion of its semi-annual meeting (1745/1545 GMT). Topics include "The adaptation of European housing financing systems to Central and Eastern European countries" and "The changeover to the euro". Venue: Hotel Amigo, Salle Saint-Michel, 1-3 rue de l'Amigo. Contact: Andreas J. Zehnder (49 228) 23 90 41.
WEDNESDAY, MAY 7
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Parliament Subcommittee on Monetary Affairs meets (0930/0730 GMT); European Monetary Institute (EMI) President Alexandre Lamfalussy presents EMI's annual report.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Parliament Socialist Group holds meeting on "Peace and democracy in Algeria"; press opportunity at 1700/1500 GMT. Venue: European Parliament, Leopold 5B01. Contact: Marco Piantini (322) 284 3452.

BRUSSELS - European Trade Union Confederation (ETUC) Secretary General Emilio Gabaglio holds news conference to present ETUC's views on the Amsterdam EU summit and its plans for a "Tour for jobs" cycle ride (1030/0830 GMT). Venue: ETUC headquarters, Auditorium 155 Blvd Emile Jacqmain. Contact: ETUC (322) 224 0411.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Euro Citizen Action Group holds news conference on the outcome of the conference on "European citizenship - current state and future development" (1500/1300 GMT). Venue: International Press Centre. Contact: Tony Venables, ECAS (322) 548 0490.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Global Legislators Organisation for a Balanced Environment (GLOBE) holds its 12th general assembly (third of three days).
THURSDAY, MAY 8
- EU institutions closed for Ascension holiday.
FRIDAY, MAY 9
- EU institutions closed for "Robert Schuman" remembrance day.

BRUSSELS - Final session of the inter-governmental conference (IGC) for young people, a simulation of EU treaty reform talks by pupils at Brussels schools. Venue: European Parliament, Leopold building.
SATURDAY, MAY 10
BRUSSELS - Open house at European Union buildings.

BRUSSELS - European Association of Lawyers for Democracy and World Human Rights (EALDH) holds conference on "Environmental law in Europe" (1300/1100 GMT). Venue: German Land Hessen Representation to the EU.
SUNDAY, MAY 11
No events scheduled.
